title: CT 105 (download-client): route it through the AirVPN WireGuard tunnel with a kill-switch
description:
Operator decision 2026-10-11: the download client's traffic goes only through AirVPN; if the tunnel is down, nothing leaves on the home connection (a kill-switch).

Measured 2026-10-11: CT 105 (download-client, 192.168.1.24) has no VPN — interfaces lo and eth0 only, no /etc/wireguard, no wg-quick unit, default route via 192.168.1.1, and a global IPv6 address; qBittorrent (qbittorrent-nox.service, Web UI on 8080, torrent port 61661) sends its traffic on the home connection (public IPv4 198.51.100.7). The AirVPN WireGuard config is stored in the engine as the secret AIRVPN_WG_CONF (Switzerland, ch3 entry3, UDP 1637). CT 105 is unprivileged (features: nesting=1).

Inside CT 105: install wireguard-tools, write the stored AirVPN config ($AIRVPN_WG_CONF, never as a literal) to /etc/wireguard/wg0.conf with mode 600, and bring it up with wg-quick at boot (wg-quick@wg0, enabled). Add a kill-switch in the container's own firewall so that, apart from the LAN (192.168.1.0/24 — the Web UI on 8080 stays reachable from home) and the VPN endpoint itself, no IPv4 or IPv6 traffic leaves through eth0; it must persist across reboots. If WireGuard cannot create its interface inside this unprivileged container, say so with the error and stop.

Done when `pct exec 105 -- wg show` lists the wg0 peer with a recent handshake, `pct exec 105 -- curl -4 -s --max-time 15 https://api.ipify.org` prints an address that is NOT 198.51.100.7, and `pct exec 105 -- curl -6 -s --max-time 10 https://api6.ipify.org` prints nothing or the tunnel's address, never the home IPv6.
